rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.e1: Defence: now with Black. White has the pawn on h5 and the bishop on f1, which moves on the light squares.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.e2: The pawn promotes on h8, a dark square, which this bishop does not control. It is the wrong bishop for the h-pawn.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.e3: With a rook pawn and the wrong bishop, the king that reaches the corner cannot be driven out, and the game ends in a draw.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.p: Play as Black: which way does the king go?
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.certo: Yes. The king goes to f8, on its way to g8 and h8.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the king to f8: it heads for g8 and h8, the corner the bishop does not control.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.err.e8: The king goes to d8, away from the corner.
With this move White has a resource: the white king goes to f7, shuts the way to the corner, and the pawn runs.
Back to the position: look for the move that brings the king closer to h8.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.fora: With that move the king moves away from h8. Look for the way to the corner.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: which way is the corner?
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.l1: Attack: the pawn advances to h6, heading for h8.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.l2: Defence: the king reaches g8, next to the corner.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.l3: Attack: the white king comes to f6 and takes g7 away from the black king.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex1.l4: Defence: the king reaches h8, the square the bishop does not control. With the king in the corner, the game is a draw.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: now with White, again the h-pawn and the light-squared bishop. The black king on f8 is two steps from h8.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.e2: With the wrong bishop, your chance is to keep the black king out of the corner: shut the way through g8 and g7.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.p: Play as White: how do you shut the way to the corner?
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.certo: Yes. The king on h7 controls g8 and g7, and the black king cannot enter the corner.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is the king to h7: it controls g8 and g7, and the black king cannot enter the corner.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.alt.d3: This also wins: the bishop on c4 controls g8, and the king on g6 controls g7. The black king stays out of the corner.
In the line, follow the other winning move: the king goes to h7 and controls the same squares.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.err.h5: The pawn advances to h6, but g8 is still free for the black king.
With this move Black has a resource: the king reaches g8, next to the corner, and never leaves it.
Back to the position: look for the move that takes g8 away from the black king.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.err.g6: The king goes to f6, and g8 is still free for the black king.
With this move Black has a resource: the king reaches g8, next to the corner, and never leaves it.
Back to the position: look for the move that takes g8 away from the black king.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.fora: With that move the black king reaches g8 and the corner. Look for the move that takes g8 away from it.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: the black king must not reach g8.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.l0: The king goes to h7 and controls g8 and g7.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.l1: Defence: the black king comes to f7, but g8 and g7 are controlled by the white king.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.l2: Attack: the pawn advances to h6, heading for h8.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.l3: Defence: the black king goes back to f8, as close to the corner as it can get.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.l4: Attack: the bishop goes to g6 and takes f7 away from the black king.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.l5: Defence: the black king has only e7 and moves away from the corner.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.ideia.ex2.l6: Attack: the king goes to g7, and the pawn goes on to h8. Here, with the black king out of the corner, the wrong bishop wins.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.barcza.1: Defence: in Zurich, in 1959, Barcza, with White, was left with a lone king against Fischer's pawn on a5. The game ended in a draw here.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.barcza.2: The a-pawn promotes on a1, in the corner. If the white king reaches that corner, the pawn cannot get through. Which way does the king get there?
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.barcza.3: The king goes to d2, on its way to c1. It is the only move that draws.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.barcza.4: Attack: the black king comes to b3, in front of the pawn.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.barcza.5: Defence: the white king reaches c1.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.barcza.6: Attack: the pawn advances to a4, on its way to a1.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.barcza.7: Defence: the king goes to b1, right next to the corner.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.barcza.8: Attack: the pawn reaches a3; Black has no other plan.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.barcza.9: Defence: the white king enters the corner, on a1. Against a lone rook pawn, the king that reaches the corner draws.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.taimanov.1: Defence: in Vancouver, in 1971, Fischer, with White, faced Taimanov. Black has only the knight against the bishop and the h-pawn.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.taimanov.2: The pawn promotes on h8, a dark square, and the bishop on g4 moves on the light ones: it is the wrong bishop.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.taimanov.3: If the knight leaves the board, that ending remains, and the black king in the corner draws. The plan is to bring the king to h8, even giving up the knight.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.taimanov.4: The knight goes to d3, heading for f4.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.taimanov.5: Attack: the pawn advances to h4, heading for h8.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.taimanov.6: Defence: the knight reaches f4 and controls h5, the pawn's next square.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.taimanov.7: Attack: the white king goes to f5 and attacks the knight.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.taimanov.8: Defence: the black king goes to d6 and lets the knight be captured.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.taimanov.9: Attack: the white king captures the knight.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.taimanov.1: Defence: the black king goes on to e7, on its way to f8 and h8. The wrong bishop is left, and the king reaches the corner: a draw.
In the game, Taimanov took his king to e4, away from the corner. Fischer took f5 away from it with the bishop on c8 and won.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.excecao.1: Attack: in Buenos Aires, in 1968, Panno, with White, was left with the h-pawn against Najdorf's king. Both kings are far from the corner.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.excecao.2: Here the corner does not save Black if the white king reaches g7 first: from there it controls g8 and h8, and the pawn promotes.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.excecao.3: Count the moves: the white king needs four to reach g7, the black king four to reach f8, and it is White to move.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.excecao.4: The king goes to g4 and climbs the g-file.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.excecao.5: Defence: the black king runs along the seventh rank, to c7.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.excecao.6: Attack: the king reaches g5. Here Najdorf resigned; the rest is analysis.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.excecao.7: Defence: the black king comes to d7, on its way to f8.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.excecao.8: Attack: the white king reaches g6.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.excecao.9: Defence: the black king comes to e7, one step from f8.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.demos.excecao.10: Attack: the white king reaches g7 first and controls g8 and h8. Here, with the attacking king in front of the pawn and the black king far from it, the attack wins.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.pratica.valeAqui: Now with White, with just the pawn on h6. The black king is near the corner. Does it draw here? Remember that the pawn also controls squares. Play as White and find the best move.
The pawn went to h7 and took g8 away from the black king. With your king on g6, controlling f7 and g7, the black king cannot reach the corner, and the pawn promotes.
The king goes to h7 and gets stuck in the corner: the black king comes to f7, and your king only has h8. A draw.
The king goes to f6, and the black king steps onto g8, next to the corner. A draw.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.pratica.chave.en: Now with Black, a-pawn against a-pawn. The white king on e3 is far from the a1 corner. Play as Black and get your king in front of your pawn before it.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.pratica.chave.fi: Your king captured the pawn on a3 and reached b2, next to a1 and in front of your pawn, before the white king: it cannot reach the corner, and the pawn promotes.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.pratica.chave.er: The pawn advances to a4 too early, and the white king gains time: it comes to c1 and b1 and reaches the corner. A draw.
The king goes to c4 and leaves the pawn on a3. The white king comes to d2, on its way to b1 and the corner: a draw.
The king goes to b3, but c1 and b1 stay free: the white king comes to c1 and reaches the corner. A draw.
The pawn advances to a4 too early: the white king comes to c2 and takes b2 away from your king. It reaches the corner, and it is a draw.
The king goes to a2, on the pawn's path, and c1 stays free: the white king comes to c1 and traps your king in the corner. A draw.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.pratica.fechar.e: Now with the light-squared bishop and the pawn on h3, the wrong bishop. The black king on g5 wants to reach h8. Play as White and do not let it.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.pratica.fechar.f: Your king got near the corner before the black king and shut the way to h8. Out of the corner, the black king cannot stop the pawn, and the wrong bishop wins.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.pratica.fechar.e: The king goes to e6 and stays far from the corner. The black king comes to h6 and then to h7 and h8: a draw.
The pawn advances to h4 with check, and the black king captures it. Without the pawn there is no way to win: a draw.
The king goes to d6 and moves away from the corner. The black king comes to h6 and then to h7 and h8: a draw.
The pawn advances, but the king has not shut the corner yet: the black king comes to h7 and then to h8. A draw. First shut the way to h8.
The king goes back to e7 and moves away from the corner: the black king comes to h7 and then to h8. A draw.
The king goes to f6 and leaves g8 and h7 free: the black king comes to h7 and reaches the corner. A draw.
The king goes back to f7 and leaves h7 free: the black king comes to h7, next to the corner. A draw.
rot.rookPawnWrongBishop.pratica.cantoBis: Now the defence: Black has the pawn on a4 and the light-squared bishop, and the pawn promotes on a1, a dark square. Play as White and draw.
Your king reached b1, next to the corner, and stays between a1 and b1. The light-squared bishop does not control a1, and the pawn cannot get through: a draw.
The king goes to c1, but the black king comes to b3 and the bishop on a2 controls b1: your king cannot enter the corner, and the pawn promotes.
The king goes to c3, but the bishop comes to b1 and shuts the way to the corner: the pawn promotes.
The king steps out to c3, away from the corner: the black king comes to a2, and the pawn promotes.
The king goes to c1, away from a1: the black king comes to a2, and your king cannot get back to the corner. The pawn promotes.
